name: Sovereign Body: A Manifesto Against the Chrome Mandate
creator: The Unclocked Collective (attributed; no individual author claimed)
description: A banned manifesto arguing that corponation-mandated BCI implants for certain employment tiers constitute a form of bodily sovereignty violation equivalent to historical forced medical procedures, drawing explicit and detailed parallels to colonial-era medical experimentation documented across multiple continents. The text is legally classified as 'incitement to infrastructure refusal' under Meridian Civic Code 7.14 and cannot be legally distributed, stored, or quoted at length. It circulates on the Shelf as printed single-sheet folded pamphlets and as encrypted neural feed fragments.
medium: underground print (pamphlet format); encrypted neural feed fragments; physical full copies extremely rare
cultural_impact: Galvanized the BCI refuser movement and contributed directly to a 2216 work stoppage in Shelf-adjacent logistics sectors; the Meridian Civic Authority's response to that stoppage is considered one of the more significant labor crackdowns of the decade.
controversy: The manifesto is the manifesto — its existence is the controversy. Civic Authority has arrested over 300 people for distribution. Several attributed co-authors have been identified and prosecuted; the Unclocked Collective denies these identifications are accurate. There is genuine debate within social justice communities about whether the text's tactics help or endanger Shelf residents.
story_hooks: A complete physical copy of the manifesto has surfaced in a Tier 4 antiquarian bookshop — someone is trying to sell it, which means someone brought it up from the Shelf, and that person is now in serious danger.

The manifesto contains a specific legal argument in its appendix that, if filed correctly, could actually succeed in challenging the BCI employment mandate — but doing so would require a Tier 4 lawyer willing to attach their name to it.

One of the 300 arrested distributors was not actually involved with the Unclocked Collective — they were framed, and the evidence of that framing is encoded in the text itself for those who know how to read it.
